Viral and bacterial disease trends after COVID-19

Stakeholder report · public health expert

Question: How have viral and bacterial infectious diseases in Switzerland developed in the years after COVID (2021-2025)?

Source: FOPH Infectious Disease Dashboard (IDD) exports, published up to 2026-09-30. National level (CH + FL), all ages, all sexes. Period 2021–2025, reference year 2019.

Headline numbers

Viral (excl. COVID-19) vs 2019

+123%

2021→2025: +1213%

Bacterial vs 2019

+23%

2021→2025: +32%

COVID-19 notifications

-98%

peak 2022: 3,045,024

Strongest rise

Influenza

+7851% since 2021

Key findings

  • Bacterial notifications changed +32% between 2021 and 2025 and are +23% vs 2019. Main contributors: Shigellosis, Gonorrhoea, Lyme borreliosis.
  • Viral notifications excluding COVID-19 changed +1213% between 2021 and 2025.
  • Excluding Influenza as well, viral notifications are -4% vs 2019.
  • Largest relative increases: Influenza +7851%; Shigellosis +134%; Hepatitis A +74%.
  • Largest decreases: COVID-19 * -98%; Hepatitis E -48%.
